userStories.title: Add healer protocol interface to standardize hasattr checks
acceptanceCriteria: Create a HealerProtocol (typing.Protocol) in src/agents/base.py with optional methods: reset_backoff(), preflight_check(), backoff_time property, retry_count property, cache_was_cleaned property
Update orchestrator.py to use isinstance(healer, HealerProtocol) instead of hasattr() checks at lines ~192, 404, 1700, 1779-1783
Update runner.py to use protocol checks instead of hasattr() at line ~352
All existing tests in tests/test_healer_base.py continue to pass
Add test that verifies each healer class satisfies the protocol
userStories.notes: Tier: Refactoring. DONE: Created SupportsBackoff and SupportsPreflight runtime_checkable Protocols in base.py. Replaced 6 hasattr() calls with isinstance() in orchestrator.py (_init_event_subscriptions, run_preflight, reset, _serialize_healer_states, _restore_healer_states) and 1 in runner.py (_reset_healers). cache_was_cleaned kept as hasattr since it's a data-only attribute (runtime_checkable only checks methods pre-Python 3.12). Added 7 protocol satisfaction tests. All 41 test_healer_base tests pass.

userStories.title: Add checkpoint backup JSON schema validation before restore
acceptanceCriteria: In CheckpointHealer._restore_from_backup(), validate that the backup JSON has required keys (last_completed_stage, stages, timestamp) before overwriting the live checkpoint
If backup validation fails, log the specific missing/invalid keys and return HealerResult.failed() instead of silently restoring corrupt data
Add a _validate_checkpoint_schema() method that checks for required fields and valid stage names from STAGE_ORDER
Add unit test for successful validation of a well-formed backup
Add unit test for failed validation when backup is missing required keys
Add unit test for failed validation when backup has invalid stage names
userStories.notes: Tier: Bug prevention. DONE: Added _validate_checkpoint_schema() to CheckpointHealer that checks required keys (last_completed_stage, stages, timestamp), validates last_completed_stage against STAGE_ORDER, validates all stage dict keys, and checks stages is a dict. Modified _restore_from_backup() to call validation before restore, returning HealerResult.failed() with validation_errors detail on failure. 15 tests in test_checkpoint_schema_validation.py cover success, missing keys, invalid stages, and integration with restore. All 68 existing healer+checkpoint tests still pass.

userStories.title: Add circuit breaker to watcher agent for repeated classification failures
acceptanceCriteria: In WatcherAgent, track consecutive classification failures where confidence < 0.3 (currently only tracks Ollama connectivity failures)
After 5 low-confidence classifications in a row, disable watcher and fall through to pattern routing for 10 minutes
Log a warning when circuit breaker trips with the failure count and cooldown duration
Add reset_circuit_breaker() method that can be called externally to re-enable the watcher
Add unit test that verifies circuit breaker trips after 5 low-confidence results
Add unit test that verifies circuit breaker auto-resets after cooldown period
userStories.notes: Tier: Reliability. DONE: Added low-confidence circuit breaker to WatcherAgent (watcher.py). Tracks consecutive classifications with confidence < 0.3; trips after 5 in a row, disabling watcher for 600s cooldown with auto-reset. Added is_circuit_breaker_tripped(), reset_circuit_breaker(), _record_low_confidence(), _record_good_confidence() methods. classify_error() checks breaker before calling LLM. 10 tests in test_watcher_circuit_breaker.py: trips after 5, returns None when tripped, good confidence resets counter, boundary check, end-to-end classify flow, auto-reset after cooldown, still tripped during cooldown, classify works after reset, manual reset, safe reset when not tripped.

userStories.title: Standardize config access pattern across all healers
acceptanceCriteria: Add a get_config_value(config_obj, field_name, default) helper function to src/agents/base.py that handles both dict and object access (Rule 6)
Replace mixed hasattr/isinstance/dict-get patterns in api.py (lines ~187-245), caption.py (lines ~502-521), and download.py (lines ~402-404) with the new helper
Helper handles None config objects by returning the default value
Add unit test for helper with dict config input
Add unit test for helper with dataclass config input
Add unit test for helper with None config input
userStories.notes: Tier: Refactoring. DONE: Added get_config_value() and set_config_value() helpers to agents/base.py. get_config_value handles dict (.get), object (getattr), and None (returns default). set_config_value handles dict ([]=), object (setattr), and None (returns False). Replaced 7 mixed hasattr/isinstance patterns: api.py _handle_timeout and _try_provider_switch (2 sites), caption.py _enable_auto_captions and _update_config_for_auto_subs (2 sites), download.py _handle_format_error, _handle_network_error, _handle_incomplete (3 sites). 12 tests in test_healer_config_helpers.py: 8 for get_config_value (dict, dataclass, None, missing key, falsy values), 4 for set_config_value (dict, new key, dataclass, None). All pass.

userStories.title: Add fallback chain pattern routing for embedding and LLM provider errors

Each new pattern group has at least 3 regex alternatives
Add unit test that verifies each new pattern matches its intended error message
Existing pattern routing tests continue to pass
userStories.notes: Added 9 new patterns (3 embedding dimension→api-healer, 3 LLM JSON→api-healer, 3 transcription→transcription-healer). 19 new tests, all 113 fallback tests pass. Committed as 1cc0d92.

userStories.title: Add healer timeout enforcement with configurable per-healer limits
acceptanceCriteria: In HealingOrchestrator.coordinate_heal(), wrap each healer.fix() call with a timeout using the per-healer timeouts already defined in the orchestrator (api-healer: 120s, download-healer: 60s, etc.)
If a healer exceeds its timeout, log a warning and return HealerResult.failed() with reason 'timeout'
Use threading.Timer or signal-based timeout (compatible with Windows) to enforce the limit
Add test that verifies a slow healer is terminated after its configured timeout
Add test that verifies the timeout value is read from the healer_timeouts dict correctly
Existing healer timeout tests in test_healer_timeout.py continue to pass
userStories.notes: Tier: Reliability. Files: src/agents/orchestrator.py (modify coordinate_heal ~line 900-1050 where healer.fix() is called, use existing healer_timeouts dict defined at ~line 450). The per-healer timeouts are defined but the actual timeout enforcement mechanism may not be wrapping every fix() call path, allowing a stuck healer to block the entire healing pipeline.
